title: Suspense and asynchronous UI
description: Learn how Suspense lets you declare loading states for asynchronous operations and coordinate multiple async UI regions.

data.text: Suspense lets you wrap a part of your UI in a boundary and show a fallback while that part loads. It works for both **code splitting** with `React.lazy` and **data fetching** with frameworks that integrate with React's Suspense integration.

When a component inside a Suspense boundary throws a promise — either from a lazy chunk or a data fetch — React catches it, displays the fallback, and retries rendering the subtree once the promise resolves. The rest of the UI remains interactive during this time.

items: A component suspends by throwing a promise or a thenable
React shows the nearest fallback UI
When the promise resolves, React retries the suspended component
If multiple boundaries suspend, they resolve independently

data.title: Lazy loading a component
data.content: Wrap the dynamic import in React.lazy and provide a fallback while the chunk downloads.

data.text: Modern data-fetching libraries like React Router, Relay, and Next.js App Router expose a Suspense-enabled API. Instead of `useEffect` to fetch, you read data directly in the render path. If the data is not ready, the component suspends and React shows the fallback.

data.title: Suspense-enabled data fetch (conceptual)
data.content: This example shows the pattern: read data synchronously, suspend if missing.

data.text: When several async regions load at once, you can use `SuspenseList` to show them together or reveal them in order. This prevents layout shifts and creates a more polished loading experience.

items: Nested Suspense boundaries can show partial content while deeper parts load

data.title: Avoid waterfalls with parallel fetches
data.text: If each Suspense boundary starts its fetch inside the component, requests chain sequentially. Start fetches in parallel at a higher level and pass promises down to keep load times low.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Suspense turns asynchronous operations into declarative UI states
Throwing a promise suspends rendering until it resolves
Fallbacks keep the rest of the UI interactive
Coordinate multiple boundaries to avoid layout shifts
data.takeaway: Suspense is most powerful when combined with parallel data loading and thoughtful fallback design.
